timelines.title: American History
timelines.description: Explore important events in American history, from independence to the Civil Rights Movement.

events.title: Declaration of Independence
events.description: The thirteen colonies declared independence from Great Britain.

events.title: American Revolution Ends
events.description: The Treaty of Paris formally ended the American Revolutionary War.

events.title: U.S. Constitution Signed
events.description: Delegates at the Constitutional Convention signed the new framework of government.

events.title: Louisiana Purchase
events.description: The United States bought territory from France, roughly doubling the nation's size.

events.title: American Civil War Begins
events.description: Confederate forces attacked Fort Sumter.

events.title: Emancipation Proclamation
events.description: President Lincoln declared enslaved people in Confederate-held territory to be free.

events.title: Civil War Ends
events.description: Confederate General Robert E. Lee surrendered to Ulysses S. Grant at Appomattox Court House.

events.title: Transcontinental Railroad Completed
events.description: The Central Pacific and Union Pacific railroads met at Promontory Summit, Utah, linking the coasts.

events.title: Ellis Island Opens
events.description: Ellis Island became the main immigration station as industrial growth drew millions to the United States.

events.title: Brown v. Board of Education
events.description: The Supreme Court ruled that racial segregation in public schools was unconstitutional.

events.title: Montgomery Bus Boycott Begins
events.description: Following Rosa Parks's arrest, Black residents of Montgomery began a year-long boycott of city buses.

events.title: March on Washington
events.description: Hundreds of thousands gathered for jobs and freedom, where Martin Luther King Jr. gave his "I Have a Dream" speech.

events.title: Civil Rights Act Signed
events.description: The law outlawed discrimination based on race, color, religion, sex, or national origin.

events.title: Voting Rights Act Signed
events.description: The law prohibited racial discrimination in voting practices.

timelines.title: Ancient Civilizations
timelines.description: Explore the rise of early civilizations in Mesopotamia, Egypt, Greece, and Rome.

events.title: Rise of Sumerian City-States
events.description: Cities such as Uruk emerged in southern Mesopotamia, among the world's earliest urban centers.

events.title: Cuneiform Writing Develops
events.description: Sumerians developed cuneiform, one of the earliest known writing systems.

events.title: Unification of Egypt
events.description: Upper and Lower Egypt were traditionally united under the first pharaoh.

events.title: Great Pyramid of Giza Built
events.description: Pharaoh Khufu's pyramid was completed and became the largest of Egypt's pyramids.

events.title: Code of Hammurabi
events.description: Babylonian king Hammurabi issued one of the earliest and most complete written law codes.

events.title: Battle of Kadesh
events.description: Egypt under Ramses II fought the Hittite Empire in one of the earliest well-documented battles.

events.title: First Ancient Olympic Games
events.description: The traditional date of the first Olympic Games, held in Olympia, Greece.

events.title: Traditional Founding of Rome
events.description: According to Roman tradition, Romulus founded Rome.

events.title: Persia Conquers Babylon
events.description: Cyrus the Great captured Babylon, bringing Mesopotamia into the Persian Empire.

events.title: Roman Republic Established
events.description: The Roman monarchy was traditionally considered to have been overthrown.

events.title: Battle of Marathon
events.description: Athenian forces defeated a Persian invasion in a landmark Greek victory.

events.title: Parthenon Construction Begins
events.description: Athens began building the Parthenon during the height of its golden age.

events.title: Death of Alexander the Great
events.description: Alexander died in Babylon, and his vast empire soon fractured among his generals.

events.title: Death of Cleopatra VII
events.description: Egypt's last Ptolemaic ruler died, and Egypt became a Roman province.

events.title: Roman Empire Begins
events.description: Augustus became the first Roman emperor.

timelines.title: Medieval History
timelines.description: Explore the Middle Ages, from the fall of Rome to the dawn of the Renaissance.

events.title: Fall of the Western Roman Empire
events.description: The last Western Roman emperor, Romulus Augustulus, was deposed.

events.title: Charlemagne Crowned Emperor
events.description: Pope Leo III crowned Charlemagne emperor of the Romans in Rome.

events.title: Death of Charlemagne
events.description: Charlemagne died, and his empire was later divided among his heirs.

events.title: Battle of Hastings
events.description: William of Normandy defeated King Harold II and began the Norman conquest of England.

events.title: First Crusade Launched
events.description: Pope Urban II called for a military expedition to the Holy Land at the Council of Clermont.

events.title: Crusaders Capture Jerusalem
events.description: Crusader forces took Jerusalem at the end of the First Crusade.

events.title: Magna Carta Sealed
events.description: King John of England agreed to limits on royal power in a charter of rights.

events.title: Black Death Reaches Europe
events.description: The plague arrived by ship in Sicily and went on to kill a large share of Europe's population.

events.title: Brunelleschi's Dome Completed
events.description: The dome of Florence Cathedral was completed, a signature achievement of the early Italian Renaissance.

events.title: Fall of Constantinople
events.description: The Ottoman Empire captured Constantinople, ending the Byzantine Empire.

events.title: Michelangelo Completes David
events.description: Michelangelo finished his marble statue in Florence, a landmark of Renaissance art.

timelines.title: World Wars
timelines.description: Explore the two world wars, the years between them, and the postwar order.

events.title: Assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand
events.description: The Austro-Hungarian heir was killed in Sarajevo, setting off the July Crisis.

events.title: World War I Begins
events.description: Austria-Hungary declared war on Serbia, and the major powers were soon drawn in.

events.title: United States Enters World War I
events.description: The U.S. declared war on Germany.

events.title: Armistice of 1918
events.description: Fighting on the Western Front ended with an armistice between the Allies and Germany.

events.title: Treaty of Versailles
events.description: The peace treaty formally ended the war with Germany and imposed heavy terms.

events.title: Wall Street Crash
events.description: The stock market collapse helped trigger the Great Depression, straining economies and politics worldwide.

events.title: Hitler Becomes Chancellor
events.description: Adolf Hitler was appointed chancellor of Germany, and the Nazi regime soon consolidated power.

events.title: World War II Begins
events.description: Germany invaded Poland, and Britain and France declared war two days later.

events.title: Battle of Britain
events.description: The Royal Air Force defended Britain against the German Luftwaffe.

events.title: Attack on Pearl Harbor
events.description: Japan attacked the U.S. naval base in Hawaii, bringing the United States into World War II.

events.title: Battle of Midway
events.description: U.S. naval forces sank four Japanese aircraft carriers in a turning point in the Pacific.

events.title: Battle of Stalingrad Ends
events.description: German forces surrendered at Stalingrad after months of fighting, a major turning point on the Eastern Front.

events.title: D-Day Invasion of Normandy
events.description: Allied forces landed on the beaches of Normandy, opening a Western Front in France.

events.title: Victory in Europe
events.description: Germany's surrender took effect, ending the war in Europe.

events.title: Atomic Bombings and Japan's Surrender
events.description: Atomic bombs were dropped on Hiroshima and Nagasaki, and Japan formally surrendered on September 2.

events.title: United Nations Founded
events.description: The UN Charter came into force, creating an organization aimed at preserving international peace.

events.title: Marshall Plan Enacted
events.description: The U.S. approved major aid to help rebuild Western European economies.

events.title: NATO Founded
events.description: Western nations signed the North Atlantic Treaty, forming a collective defense alliance.

timelines.title: History of Exploration
timelines.description: Explore voyages, scientific discoveries, flight, and the race to space.

events.title: Dias Rounds the Cape of Good Hope
events.description: Portuguese navigator Bartolomeu Dias sailed around southern Africa, opening a sea route toward Asia.

events.title: Columbus Reaches the Americas
events.description: Christopher Columbus made landfall in the Caribbean on his first Atlantic voyage.

events.title: Da Gama Reaches India
events.description: Vasco da Gama arrived at Calicut, establishing a sea route from Europe to India.

events.title: Magellan Expedition Circumnavigates the Globe
events.description: The surviving ship of Magellan's expedition returned to Spain, completing the first voyage around the world.

events.title: Copernicus Publishes His Heliocentric Model
events.description: Nicolaus Copernicus proposed that the Earth orbits the Sun, a cornerstone of the Scientific Revolution.

events.title: Galileo's Telescope Observations
events.description: Galileo reported moons orbiting Jupiter and other discoveries made with a telescope.

events.title: Newton Publishes the Principia
events.description: Isaac Newton laid out the laws of motion and universal gravitation.

events.title: Cook's First Pacific Voyage
events.description: James Cook charted New Zealand and the east coast of Australia and observed the transit of Venus.

events.title: Darwin Publishes On the Origin of Species
events.description: Charles Darwin presented the theory of evolution by natural selection.

events.title: Wright Brothers' First Powered Flight
events.description: Orville and Wilbur Wright made the first sustained, controlled powered airplane flights at Kitty Hawk, North Carolina.

events.title: Amundsen Reaches the South Pole
events.description: Roald Amundsen's Norwegian expedition became the first to reach the South Pole.

events.title: Lindbergh's Solo Transatlantic Flight
events.description: Charles Lindbergh flew nonstop from New York to Paris in the Spirit of St. Louis.

events.title: Sputnik 1 Launched
events.description: The Soviet Union launched the first artificial satellite, beginning the Space Race.

events.title: Yuri Gagarin Orbits Earth
events.description: Soviet cosmonaut Yuri Gagarin became the first human in space.

events.title: Apollo 11 Moon Landing
events.description: Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin became the first humans to walk on the Moon.

events.title: Hubble Space Telescope Launched
events.description: The orbiting observatory began transforming our view of the universe.

timelines.title: History of Technology
timelines.description: Explore inventions that reshaped communication, industry, and daily life.

events.title: Gutenberg's Printing Press
events.description: Johannes Gutenberg developed movable-type printing in Europe, making books far cheaper to produce.

events.title: Watt's Improved Steam Engine
events.description: James Watt patented a more efficient steam engine that powered the Industrial Revolution.

events.title: Voltaic Pile Invented
events.description: Alessandro Volta created the first electric battery, providing a steady source of electric current.

events.title: Faraday Discovers Electromagnetic Induction
events.description: Michael Faraday's discovery laid the foundation for electric generators and motors.

events.title: First Telegraph Message
events.description: Samuel Morse sent "What hath God wrought" from Washington to Baltimore, launching long-distance electrical communication.

events.title: Bell Patents the Telephone
events.description: Alexander Graham Bell received a patent for the telephone.

events.title: Edison's Practical Light Bulb
events.description: Thomas Edison's team demonstrated a long-lasting incandescent lamp.

events.title: Pearl Street Station Opens
events.description: Edison's power station in New York City began supplying electricity to customers.

events.title: Marconi's Transatlantic Radio Signal
events.description: Guglielmo Marconi reported receiving a wireless signal sent across the Atlantic Ocean.

events.title: Ford Introduces the Model T
events.description: The affordable automobile, later mass-produced on assembly lines, put cars within reach of ordinary families.

events.title: ENIAC Unveiled
events.description: One of the first general-purpose electronic computers was publicly announced at the University of Pennsylvania.

events.title: Transistor Invented
events.description: Bell Labs researchers demonstrated the transistor, the building block of modern electronics.

events.title: First ARPANET Message
events.description: The first message was sent between computers on ARPANET, a forerunner of the internet.

events.title: IBM Personal Computer Released
events.description: IBM's PC helped bring personal computing into homes and offices.

events.title: World Wide Web Opens to the Public
events.description: Tim Berners-Lee's web became publicly available, making the internet far easier to navigate.

events.title: iPhone Announced
events.description: Apple unveiled the iPhone, popularizing the modern touchscreen smartphone.
